answer: To claim a seat, lock a stake and register one HTTPS callback. A random falcon sentinel issues an unpredictable nonce that must be signed and returned from that exact TLS certificate within 800ms. Each certificate fingerprint and routed prefix maps to only one seat, so shared proxies fail uniqueness and latency checks. The fable that a key is an identity dies here: without a uniquely pingable, bonded endpoint the key earns nothing. Forging N aliases costs N routes, N certificates, N always-on responders and N stakes, not one dune of scripts on a shared host.
